verses.text: It took Solomon twenty years to build the LORD's temple and his own palace.
Then Solomon rebuilt the towns Huram had given him, and he had Israelites settle in them.
Solomon went to Hamath Zobah and captured it.
He built Tadmor in the desert, and all the storage towns he built in Hamath.
He rebuilt Upper Beth Horon and Lower Beth Horon, strong cities with walls, gates, and bars.
He also built Baalath, all his storage towns, and all the towns for his chariots and horses. He built whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout all the land he ruled.
There were still people left from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. These people were not Israelites.
They were descendants of those the Israelites had not destroyed in the land. Solomon forced them to be slave workers, as they still are today.
But Solomon did not make slaves of any Israelites for his work. They were his soldiers, the chiefs of his officers, and the commanders of his chariots and horsemen.
They were also King Solomon's chief officials, two hundred and fifty of them, who were in charge of the people.

Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the City of David to the palace he had built for her. He said, "My wife must not live in the palace of David king of Israel, because the places where the LORD's ark has been are holy."
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the LORD's altar he had built in front of the temple porch.

He did this according to what was required each day, following the commands of Moses for Sabbaths, New Moons, and the three yearly festivals: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Shelters.

Following the instructions of his father David, he appointed the groups of priests for their service, and the Levites for their duties of leading praise and helping the priests, as each day required. He also appointed the gatekeepers by their groups for each gate, because this is what David, the man of God, had commanded.
They did not turn away from anything the king commanded the priests and Levites, including the care of the treasuries.
So all of Solomon's work was carried out, from the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid until it was finished. So the LORD's temple was completed.
Then Solomon went to Ezion Geber and Elath on the coast of Edom.
Huram sent him ships commanded by his own officers, men who knew the sea. They sailed with Solomon's men to Ophir and brought back about fifteen tonnes of gold, which they gave to King Solomon.
